chapters.summary: James chapter 1 teaches believers to count trials as joy, to ask God in faith for wisdom, and stresses being doers of the word, not hearers only.
keyPoints: Trials are to be counted as joy, for the testing of faith produces patience.
Whoever lacks wisdom should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault - but must ask in faith.
We are to be doers of the word and not hearers only, caring for orphans and widows in their distress, and keeping ourselves unstained by the world.
chapters.application: When facing hardship, first ask God for wisdom and rely on the Lord's patience. Do not merely listen to the word - put it into practice, living out your faith by caring for others.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses that faith and works cannot be separated - genuine faith always bears the fruit of loving deeds, and faith without works is dead.
keyPoints: We must not show favoritism based on appearance, for God has chosen the poor, while the rich oppress you.
Fulfilling the royal law means loving your neighbor as yourself; but whoever breaks one point of the law is guilty of breaking all of it.
Faith without works is dead, just as the body without the spirit is dead.
chapters.application: Today, do not show favoritism toward others - love your neighbor as yourself with a heart of compassion. Faith must be demonstrated through action; let your beliefs shape every detail of your life.

chapters.summary: James chapter 3 teaches believers to be careful with their words, and distinguishes heavenly wisdom from earthly wisdom.
keyPoints: Not many should become teachers, for though the tongue is small, it can defile the whole body.
The tongue is a restless evil; praise and cursing should not come from the same mouth.
Heavenly wisdom is pure, peace-loving, gentle, and compliant, full of mercy and good fruit.
chapters.application: Before you speak today, ask the Lord for wisdom. Build others up with gentle, peaceable words, keep far from slander and rivalry, and let the likeness of Christ flow from your mouth.

chapters.summary: James chapter 4 teaches believers to humbly submit to God, avoid worldly quarrels and pride, and draw near to God to receive cleansing and grace.
keyPoints: Fights and quarrels arise from selfish desires; asking and not receiving comes from asking wrongly - turn instead to God.
Friendship with the world is enmity with God; he gives grace to the humble.
We are forbidden to criticize and judge one another, for life is fleeting, and we should depend on the Lord's plan.
chapters.application: Examine your heart, let go of selfish desire and pride, humbly draw near to God, and entrust today to him rather than presuming on tomorrow by your own judgment.

chapters.summary: James chapter 5 urges the rich to repent, encourages believers to be patient as they wait for the Lord's return, and emphasizes the power of prayer and mutual confession.
keyPoints: The rich are warned that their wealth will rot away, for their oppression and self-indulgence will bring judgment.
Believers are urged to imitate the patience of the farmer, to strengthen their hearts, to wait for the Lord's coming, and not to grumble against one another.
Believers are taught about prayer and praise, following the example of Elias, and are called to intercede for and confess their sins to one another.
chapters.application: In hardship, wait patiently for the Lord and continually entrust your burdens to him in prayer. At the same time, examine yourself, do not cling to worldly things, and live out a testimony of love for one another.
